name: Long House Valley: what each replication quirk does to the fit
description: What each of the published replication's departures from the written model does to its fit (the sum over AD 800–1350 of squared differences from the historical households): lhv-published with one quirk turned off at a time, none, or all (the documented model), over 15 seeds. Measured (release, seeds 1–15, recorded 2026-09-25): mean fit 922 516 with none off; 919 196 without aging before the death check, 1 034 221 with the farm water check, 966 794 with the uplands PDSI, 858 177 without wrapping, 975 073 with one initial corn draw, 4 328 619 with the documented endowment, 1 233 239 with fission tried without a free farm, 864 268 with adjusted initial farms, 924 814 without the occupancy leak, 922 516 with two harvest s.d.s (equal in this preset, so nothing changes) and 4 296 013 with all off. The fresh endowment matters most by far (4.7×): under the ODD's rule a new household starts with a third of its parent's corn and most do not survive. Fission needing a free farm comes next (1.34×); the rest change the fit by less than an eighth.
